title: Devin Lloyd introductory press conference | Carolina Panthers
text: I hope you're doing well today, Devin. >> I am. I am. Likewise. >> Great. Uh, over the past several years, um, the Panthers leaguewide reputation remained, uh, near the bottom in NFL PA player polls, but, uh, Dan Morgan went out and and signed three of the top uh, free agents and and made several other key moves. Number one, what attracted you to the Panthers? And is the Morgan Canales culture, is it helping change the perception players have of the Panthers franchise? >> Yeah, absolutely. Um, you know, there's a lot to, um, be attracted to when it comes to the team and ultimately that's why I ended up signing here. Um, I think there's a lot of great pieces on defense for one. Um, and obviously being, you know, a guy, a defender, you know, that was one thing that I was looking for. Um, I mean, you got a number of players, Derek Brown, JC Horn, obviously two most notable, but, um, you know, Trayvon, um, I mean, there's guys all over the defense that make plays and, you know, I just want to come in and, uh, be a part of that playmaking unit and help elevate it the most I can. Um, obviously Dave Canales, um, you know, I think he's a great head coach and he's got this team, um, playing ball the right way. And so for me, you know, I just want to come in and, uh, and do my part and help this team, uh, maximize what we can do. uh what is the what is the word on the street so to speak of of the Panthers um two other players in the league and how has it changed over the last couple years? >> Well, that that all depends on who you ask, who you talk to. I mean um it could be different depending on where you ask. I think um you know uh I guess it's not something I never necessarily really focused on. I guess you could say until I was in free agency, you know, more so players kind of focus on their team. Obviously, you look around and see who's doing what. I would say um you know, looking at the Panthers last year from the outside in, it was a talented team that, you know, had a lot of really good pieces all over the place. And I mean, just an ascending team, you know, you know, Jacksonville was like that at one point as well. um just an ascending team and you know obviously you know made it to the playoffs, hosted a home playoff game which is huge and now it's time to take that next step and so I'm really excited to be a part of taking that next step. >> Yeah, I just want to finish up with one quick hardbiting question. Um who do you have for the basketball tournament with it starting today? >> Oh shoot. I guess we'll just have to wait and see. >> You didn't fill out a bracket? >> No, I did not. >> Okay. Hey, have a good one. Thanks a lot. >> Thank you. >> Hey K, followed by David Newton. >> Hey Devin, welcome. Uh, congratulations on the contract. >> I was curious, how much did coaching from scheme to your position coach to your defensive coordinator help you kind of reach a career year last season? >> I mean, I think, you know, when you look at you talk about coaching, um, coaching helps develop players. you know, obviously every player is talented and they have skill set and now it's on coaches at all levels, you know, from high school all the way up to NFL to really help those players get the most out of the talent that they have. So, I mean, you ask me specifically. Yeah. I mean, I I great I had great coaches last year and they definitely helped me um just take a next I say, you know, I give the most credit to them. They helped me use my hands. You know, that was one thing they emphasized and really, you know, honed in pretty much every day. Every day at practice, it was use your hands, use your hands, use your hands. So, you can play violent, you can play physical in the run game, shed off blocks, make plays. That was the thing that coach Kemp and coach uh Tim Lucaboo emphasized the most. And uh that's what I give them the most credit for. And then um you know scheme wise you know it comes down to you know no matter where you're at you know having your players be in the right position to make the most plays as possible. >> And then uh in the passing game linebackers all have their specialties but you seem to excel both at both in coverage and blitzing. How much do you have to kind of weigh that within your own game? You know obviously you can make plays in coverage but you also know you can get to the quarterback. Yeah, that just comes down to the situation, you know. Obviously, um I think from a coach's lens, you want to put your playmakers in position and it's finding the best way to do that. Obviously, I won't be the only playmaker on the team. We got playmakers all over the place. So, for him, it's coach, it's, you know, how can I get all my guys going um doing what they're best at situationally. It's like, okay, you know, right now it's his time. Okay. Now, in this next series, we're going to go um you know, get him going. And just like offensive coordinator, you know, trying to get their receivers going or running backs going, defensive coordinator, same thing. You got guys all over the place. So, it's just uh situationally, you know, and uh calling in at the right time. >> Thanks. Thanks, Deon. >> Hey, Deon. David Newton with ESPN.com. Welcome to Charlotte. >> Thank I want to ask you, Luke Forner asked uh said the other day that you you were so intense in practice that you had to tell you to calm down sometimes. Uh give me an example of that and what's that say about you? >> Um specific example on I mean I just go hard at practice, you know, I really um you know try to treat practice like the game as much as I can and obviously there's there's a time and a place to you know be physical I guess you could say. Like I wouldn't necessarily see um if you're not if you're playing without pads that that's the most um as that's the smartest time to be physical, but you can always play fast. You can always play with great technique. You always play um just just flying around the field really at 100 miles an hour. And I think that's what he was referring to. Um oh, sorry, what was the second part of your question? >> Well, that was pretty much it. I wanted to also ask you too. I mean, the Jaguars didn't pick up your fifth year option. Um, how did that impact you looking elsewhere and and how things kind of turned out for you? >> Yeah, as far as the fifth year option, um, whenever I found out the news, it was just more so, okay, like um, at this point now, I know um, you know, this is effectively uh, a one-year prov like like a contract year, I guess you could say. That's what um, you know, the term that everybody says. It was more so just me understanding like, okay, after this year I'm gonna be a free agent, you know, especially with the linebacker tag and it being mixed in with pass rushers. So, um, you know, I mean, that's just, you know, the reality of it. You know, you look at that and you look at it and you're realistic with yourself. Um, but other than that, it was just more so just playing ball. I didn't put too much into it. At the end of the day, um, I just went out and attacked each day and, you know, let the day stack. And what makes you so good in coverage? >> Um, I think it's just a natural feel. You know, you're looking at the quarterback. You know, a lot of plays I made in in zone coverage and, um, you just have a feel for looking at the quarterback, know where he wants to go. I think, uh, knowing the route concepts is huge. So, it's really about getting to your landmark as quick as possible and then that allows you to play off the routes versus, um, you know, I see a lot of linebackers, what we call drifting. they're not set, their feet aren't set, and it doesn't allow them to get their feet in the uh getting their feet in the ground and make plays on the ball in the air. Um so it comes down to technique, a feel for the game, and ultimately um when the ball's in the air, it's a mentality of that's your ball. >> Appreciate it. Thank you. >> We'll go with Joe Pson followed by Alex Zitlo. >> Hey Devin, it's Joe with the Athletic. Congrats on the contract. Um, you were asked earlier about kind of your your versatile skill set and I I just wondered this ended up being kind of a a free agency for linebackers where uh a lot of y'all didn't get what the so-called experts were projecting. Was that a surprise to you given all that you do? like because you know you're not just a guy playing the run first and second down. >> It was um but that's just the way the market went this year and uh that's what it was. And then I know you said you didn't spend a lot of time obviously when you were in Jacksonville studying the Panthers, but over the course of the last week or maybe even you know in free agency when you heard they were going to be interested. Did you dig into this defense and you know what and what had your conversations with a Gerald been like in terms of your role and expanding your role? Um, I mean they were brief, uh, but I know they're excited. Um, just about, you know, obviously getting me in the defense, um, getting Jaylen in the defense and, you know, obviously all the pieces that we have. So, um, more of those talks will happen whenever, you know, we get things going at OTAAS. Um, right now it's just about getting settled in Charlotte and um, yeah, I mean, pretty much that. >> You and Jaylen were among the top three free agents any position in a lot of the rankings, including ours. Um, what was it like when when you know, you saw him come here and then a little later in the day or, you know, I guess into the evening you you follow him and what what was your reaction? >> It was exciting. I mean, you know, he's a hell of a player. Uh the way he plays the game, um he's just very aggressive and uh you know, even my my I've had coaches that that have talked about him as well and uh they agree, you know, they echo the same thing. So, I'm excited to play with him. Um and like I said, we have, you know, guys all over that I'm excited to play with as well. Um, whenever you look at our defense and, uh, you know, the things that Dan was doing and is doing actively with our team, um, you can't help but, you know, be optimistic for the future and what we're going to do on Sundays. >> Thanks, Devin. >> Hey, Devin. Alex here with the Charlotte Observer. Welcome to Charlotte, man. >> Um, I wanted to quickly follow up about the the question about your fifth year option. And I understand that you said that um you didn't put much stock to it. It wasn't like a thing that made you hung hungrier so to speak or anything like that. And I'm curious where does that I don't know level-headedness come from? >> Uh ultimately it stems in in my faith. I think everything ultimately goes back to my faith and just um understanding that's God's plan. You know, it'll never truly be how you know I envision it. um it's always going to be how he envisions it, how it plays out, and um even if it's whether it goes my way or whether it doesn't, um I know it's all going to work out. So, it's just trusting him and uh day by day uh just accepting what comes to you. Obviously, attacking each day and uh from your perspective, from my perspective, trying to get the most out of each day, but never not getting too high, not getting too low on anything that happens. Uh just trying to see things from the right lens. >> Nice. Um, and then I also wanted to ask about uh your parents were both in the Navy, correct? >> Yeah. >> Um, what I'm just curious how that impacted you uh personally and then also in your football journey. >> Yeah, the biggest thing with my parents being in the Navy um is discipline. Um, just doing all the little things right. Obviously at home um you know they're they're pretty strict so you know I think everything starts at home too. just all the little things, uh, you know, cutting the grass on Saturday mornings, having to get up on your own to cut the grass or washing cars or keeping your bathroom and your room clean, just all the little stuff, doing your homework, you know, being a good student. Um, all those things just start to add up to the point where now it's um, it's who I am. It's part of my identity, just being disciplined. And, um, nobody has to tell me to get up and and go work out, you know. Um, and over the years it's built up to, you know, now it's a part of my lifestyle. So, I'd say that's the biggest thing. >> Wonderful. Thanks, man. >> We have time for a few more. We'll go with Cass, followed by Sheena. >> Hey, Devin. How's it going? >> I'm good. I'm good. How are you doing? >> Good. Sorry, my camera is not working, so just use your imagination. Um, real curious. Just wanted to follow up on that. Did you ever consider going into the Navy? Um, I think uh there was an option at one point where coming out of high school, if I didn't go to college, it would be the Navy, but my head was so focused and I was so determined on going to college and playing football. So, that was never really option for me per se, but it was always there. It was always available. Like, that was, I guess you could say, the plan B. Um, but for me, there really was no plan B. Like, that was never anything that I really wanted to do. And then what I also really wanted to ask was Luke Forner talked about facing you in practice earlier this week and like how sometimes like he did have to tell you like dude it's not Sunday. What was that? What were those reps like from your perspective facing him and now you'll get to do it again here? >> Yeah. I mean shoot I go hard at practice and you know like I said there's a time and a place to to be smart, not be as physical. um be more technical. And I think over the years you learn, you know, especially when you're young, it's like, okay, like I'm trying to get after I'm trying to make a play and now you're more considerate, I guess you could say, your teammates as you um grow over time. There's a time and a place, but uh yeah, I go hard at practice. You know, for me, you know, you got to treat practice as much as you can, like a game depending on the situation. And so I'm sure uh yeah, he has some stories of us going at it. I mean, you know, he's a linebacker, I'm a linebacker, he's a center, so we would have a lot of battles. um you know so yeah I'm sure he brought that up. >> Hi Devin Sheenaquick on Fox Sports Radio. How are you doing this afternoon? >> I'm well. I'm well. >> Well for starters welcome to Carolina. Um I know you talked a lot about how important the lineage of linebackers in in Carolina you know affected your decision. Did Dan Morgan and him the GM being a former linebacker that had success with this particular franchise, did that weigh in on your decision at all? And how were those conversations with him? >> Yeah, I mean, that's that's a huge plus. You know, obviously uh he knows what it takes, you know, to play uh my position at a high level in this league and um just my position in general throughout his football career. And so that's a huge plus. And um I think that's why we connected because I feel like in many ways we do see the game the same. >> Um and the second just a follow-up question on that. I know uh we have heard about your tenacity and your intensity for every rep whether it's game or practice. Um and sometimes you know there's these narratives that float around during free agency draft period or whatever and things like that. Do you think that how do you view that? How do you, you know, get around that and and kind of, I guess, express who you really are as a person in addition to the player that you are on the field when it comes to shopping around during free agency? >> Uh, I'm not sure all the way what the narratives are. I don't really focus too much on that. >> Okay, perfect. Thank you. >> All right, last question. Bashtai, >> Devin, welcome to Carolina. Just a quick question. We talked about the fifthear option. Did Jacksonville express interest in in bringing you back? >> Um, uh, they there was an offer on the table. >> That's it. >> Okay. Thank you. >> All right, Devin, that's all the questions we have for you today. Thanks for taking the time to talk to us. >> All right. Thank you.
